item.title: Israel govt formation: Eisenkot, Lieberman join hands in bid to oust Netanyahu
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party has formed a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing Israel Our Home party. This alliance is pivotal as efforts to create a government without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intensify. The Knesset was sworn in without a new government after the recent election reduced Netanyahu's majority. Eisenkot aims to establish a government by December 6, with an extension option available.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: West Virginia town sues to save 12 historic buildings from demolition in national park
item.description: Thurmond, a historic railroad town in West Virginia, is in a legal battle against the National Park Service. The lawsuit aims to halt the planned demolition of 12 historic buildings scheduled for November 30. Officials argue the agency violated federal laws and failed to consider preservation options. Concerns have also been raised regarding road safety and equipment weight limits. The court's decision will determine the future of these historic structures.

item.title: Sydney medical student identifies 5 relatives in forgotten 1965 film after social media appeal
item.description: A 1965 film uncovered in Melbourne became a bridge connecting a Sydney medical student to previously unknown relatives. This discovery showcased three generations of his family outside their residence in Mitcham. After British director Karen Walsh endeavored to uncover the family's identity, the medical student recognized his great-grandmother among the footage shared online. With the help of ABC Melbourne, the quest for family links successfully culminated.

item.title: WestJet ordered to pay Canadian couple $2,000 after 16-hour delay blamed on wind
item.description: After a grueling 16-hour delay, a Canadian couple finally made it to Vancouver, only to find themselves stuck overnight in Regina due to a missed connection. WestJet cited strong winds as the reason for the delay but could not substantiate their claim. Ultimately, the Civil Resolution Tribunal held the airline liable and awarded the couple $2,226.92 for their inconvenience, which included their legal expenses.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Colorado man freed after 27 years for infant's murder seeks $2m, but family calls claim a joke
item.description: Stephen Martinez has filed a $1.9 million claim for state compensation following his wrongful imprisonment of 27 years, a conviction now overturned. However, the family of the baby involved contests this request, deeming it inappropriate under the current circumstances. Under Colorado law, Martinez must demonstrate actual innocence to qualify for state compensation, and a judge will decide if he meets this necessary legal standard in a forthcoming ruling.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Former Texas teacher admits stealing $520,000 in tax refunds as $4m more is stopped
item.description: In a shocking turn of events, former Texas teacher Jeremy Jarod Jackson confessed to orchestrating a scheme that siphoned off $520,000 in tax refunds. He masterfully altered his company's mailing address to funnel cheques into his own hands, triggering extensive financial wrongdoing. Luckily, IRS Criminal Investigation agents intervened, blocking Jackson from cashing in on an additional $4 million in fraudulent cheques.

item.title: Giving Machines has raised $70 million; whose donations of livestock & business training helped families
item.description: The Giving Machines initiative has emerged as a worldwide project facilitating the donation of essential goods to those in need. These innovative vending machines dispense critical items like chickens, goats, and educational resources for financially struggling families. Partner organizations ensure that these donations reach their intended recipients efficiently, while also promoting women's health and girls' education across diverse areas.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New Jersey mother, son sue zoning board over rejected bayfront home plan
item.description: A New Jersey mother and her son have approached the court after a township zoning board rejected their plan to build a three-storey house on their bayfront plot. They argue that the board failed to properly consider expert evidence and the property's existing limitations. The family wants the rejection overturned and has also sought compensation, claiming that the decision effectively deprives them of the use of their land.

item.title: Utah banker mailed 37 tons of bricks to build a bank, forcing postal rule changes
item.description: In 1916, the directors of the Bank of Vernal needed bricks for a new building project. They faced high transportation costs due to poor road conditions in rural Utah. A director discovered that shipping bricks by postal service was a cheaper option, allowing many small packages to be sent. This unique approach led to changes in postal regulations regarding large shipments.

item.title: A North Carolina family donated the development rights over their 55-acre farm straddling two counties, protecting pasture and forest in a fast-growing region where most of the soil is considered prime farmland.
item.description: In North Carolina, Jennifer and Lane Tredway donated development rights to protect their 55-acre farm. This conservation easement will ensure the land remains agricultural and untouched by future development. The farm, known as Two Paths Farm, is situated in an area experiencing rapid urban expansion. Both Johnston and Wake counties are involved in preserving the agricultural character of the region.
item.dc:creator: World Desk

item.title: Woman's claim to abandoned Philadelphia house she lived in since 2003 rejected
item.description: A Philadelphia woman who claimed she had occupied an abandoned house since 2003 has lost her appeal seeking ownership through adverse possession. The Pennsylvania Superior Court dismissed her case on November 20, citing inadequate legal arguments and missing references in her appeal.
